answer: Admission proof-of-work at the atlas: each identity must solve a memory-hard puzzle averaging 2^24 hashes (~40 CPU-minutes) before it can mine or vote. Because nodes wander across the network, we bind each nonce to peer latency and a rotating crystal seed, so precomputation is useless. A 1000-identity farm burns ~28 CPU-days and ~$900 in cloud spot time; revenue stays sublinear, so the attacker hits negative ROI before 50 identities. It works because minting cost scales linearly with identities while influence stays capped.
